Topics.Title: How PreseMaker Analyzes Source Material
Topics.Summary: Explores the process by which PreseMaker reads and interprets uploaded source material to identify key themes and content areas. Learners understand what drives the AI's initial structural proposals.

Elements.Title: Uploading Source Material to PreseMaker
Elements.BodyText: The process begins when a user uploads source material into PreseMaker, providing the raw input the AI will use to build a course structure.
Elements.Notes: Source material may include documents, outlines, transcripts, or other text-based content relevant to the course subject.

Items.Text: PreseMaker accepts uploaded source material as the foundation for all subsequent analysis and structural proposals.
The quality and completeness of the uploaded material directly influences the accuracy of the AI's output.
Users should ensure source material is well-organized and representative of the full course scope before uploading.

Elements.Title: Reading and Parsing the Content
Elements.BodyText: Once material is uploaded, PreseMaker reads through the full text to parse its language, structure, and subject matter.
Elements.Notes: This parsing step is automatic and occurs before any structural suggestions are presented to the user.

Items.Text: PreseMaker scans the uploaded text to identify vocabulary, headings, and recurring concepts.
The AI breaks the content into analyzable segments to detect how ideas are grouped and sequenced.
Structural cues in the source material, such as numbered sections or headers, may guide the parsing process.

Elements.Title: Identifying Key Themes and Content Areas
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker uses its analysis to surface the dominant themes and distinct content areas present in the source material.
Elements.Notes: A theme might be a broad subject domain, while a content area represents a more specific cluster of related information within that domain.

Items.Text: The AI groups related ideas and topics together to form coherent content clusters.
Frequently appearing concepts or heavily detailed sections are weighted as primary themes.
This thematic mapping forms the conceptual backbone of the proposed module structure.

Elements.Title: Generating an Initial Structural Proposal
Elements.BodyText: Based on its thematic analysis, PreseMaker produces an initial module breakdown that reflects the key content areas it has identified.
Elements.Notes: This proposal is a starting point, not a final structure — learners are expected to review, adjust, or replace it as needed.

Items.Text: The structural proposal organizes identified themes into a logical sequence of modules.
Each proposed module corresponds to a distinct content area surfaced during analysis.
The AI's proposal is presented to the user for review before any course structure is finalized.

Elements.Title: What Drives the AI's Decisions
Elements.BodyText: Understanding the factors that influence PreseMaker's structural suggestions helps learners evaluate and refine the AI's proposals more effectively.
Elements.Notes: Awareness of these drivers empowers users to provide better source material and make more informed adjustments to the breakdown.

Items.Text: The density and depth of coverage on a topic in the source material signals its importance to the AI.
Explicit organizational markers in the source, such as chapter titles or section breaks, strongly influence module boundaries.
The AI balances breadth of topics against depth of detail to propose a structure that is both comprehensive and teachable.

Topics.Title: Understanding the AI-Suggested Module Breakdown
Topics.Summary: Introduces the initial module structure that PreseMaker proposes after analyzing source material. Learners examine what a generated breakdown looks like and what information it contains.

Elements.Title: What the AI-Generated Breakdown Looks Like
Elements.BodyText: After PreseMaker analyzes your source material, it proposes an initial module structure presented as a breakdown of the course content.
Elements.Notes: This breakdown serves as a starting point that learners can review before making any decisions about the final structure.

Items.Text: The breakdown displays a list of proposed modules, each representing a distinct chunk of the course content.
Each module entry typically includes a title and a brief description of what that module will cover.
The visual layout allows learners to quickly scan the overall scope and sequence of the proposed course.

Elements.Title: How PreseMaker Analyzes Source Material
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker processes the source material you provide and uses AI to identify logical divisions and themes within the content.
Elements.Notes: Understanding this process helps learners trust and critically evaluate the suggestions the tool produces.

Items.Text: The AI scans the source material for major topics, themes, and natural content boundaries.
It groups related ideas together to form coherent module proposals that reflect the structure of the original material.
The depth and quality of the breakdown depends on how well-organized and complete the source material is.

Elements.Title: Information Contained in Each Suggested Module
Elements.BodyText: Each module in the AI-suggested breakdown contains specific information to help you evaluate whether it is appropriate for your course.
Elements.Notes: Reviewing this information carefully is an important step before accepting or modifying the breakdown.

Items.Text: A module title summarizes the central theme or skill addressed in that section of the course.
A module description provides a brief explanation of the content scope and learning focus for that module.
Together, the title and description give enough context to judge whether the module boundaries make sense.

Elements.Title: Purpose of the Initial Breakdown
Elements.BodyText: The AI-suggested breakdown is intended as a draft structure, not a final decision, giving learners a foundation to work from.
Elements.Notes: Treating the breakdown as a starting point reduces the effort required to structure a course from scratch.

Items.Text: The initial breakdown saves time by eliminating the need to manually outline the entire course before reviewing content.
It allows learners to focus their attention on evaluating and refining structure rather than creating it from nothing.
The proposal is fully editable, meaning no part of the suggested breakdown is locked or permanent at this stage.

Elements.Title: Evaluating the Suggested Structure
Elements.BodyText: Once the breakdown is displayed, learners are expected to review it critically to determine whether the proposed modules are accurate and useful.
Elements.Notes: This evaluation step is key to ensuring the final course structure aligns with the intended learning outcomes.

Items.Text: Check whether the number of modules feels appropriate for the scope of the source material.
Assess whether each module title and description accurately reflects a meaningful and teachable chunk of content.
Look for gaps, overlaps, or misaligned groupings that may need to be corrected before moving forward.

Topics.Title: Accepting the Proposed Module Structure
Topics.Summary: Covers the workflow for reviewing and accepting the AI-generated module breakdown when it meets the course design requirements. Learners practice confirming a structure to move forward in the authoring process.

Elements.Title: Reviewing the AI-Generated Module Breakdown
Elements.BodyText: Before accepting a proposed structure, learners must carefully evaluate the AI-generated module breakdown against their course design goals.
Elements.Notes: Consider whether the number of modules is appropriate, whether the topic sequencing is logical, and whether the scope of each module aligns with learning objectives.

Items.Text: Scan each proposed module title and summary to confirm it reflects the source material accurately.
Check that the overall flow of modules supports a logical learning progression for the target audience.
Identify any gaps, redundancies, or misalignments before deciding to accept the structure.

Elements.Title: Criteria for Accepting the Structure
Elements.BodyText: A proposed module breakdown is ready to accept when it sufficiently meets the course design requirements without needing significant changes.
Elements.Notes: Not every breakdown will be perfect, but if the structure covers the key content areas and the sequencing is sound, it is generally appropriate to accept and refine later.

Items.Text: The proposed modules collectively cover all major topics present in the source material.
Module titles and descriptions are clear, distinct, and free from excessive overlap.
The number of modules is practical for the intended course length and learner audience.

Elements.Title: Performing the Accept Action in PreseMaker
Elements.BodyText: Accepting the proposed structure is a deliberate action within the PreseMaker interface that confirms the breakdown and moves the authoring process forward.
Elements.Notes: Locating and using the correct confirmation control is an important hands-on skill practiced in this topic.

Items.Text: Locate the accept or confirm option presented alongside the AI-generated module breakdown.
Select the accept action to signal that the proposed structure is approved for use.
Once confirmed, PreseMaker proceeds to initialize the course and module storage based on the accepted structure.

Elements.Title: What Happens After Acceptance
Elements.BodyText: When a learner accepts the module breakdown, PreseMaker uses that structure as the foundation for all subsequent authoring steps.
Elements.Notes: Understanding the downstream effects of acceptance helps learners appreciate why the review step is important before confirming.

Items.Text: The accepted modules are established as the working structure for the course project.
PreseMaker creates the corresponding course and module folders on disk to store all related content.
The authoring workflow advances to the next stage, where individual module content can be developed.

Elements.Title: Committing to the Structure vs. Exploring Alternatives
Elements.BodyText: Accepting the structure is a commitment to move forward, making it important to distinguish this action from options to adjust or replace the breakdown.
Elements.Notes: Learners should understand that accepting is one of several possible responses to a proposed breakdown; other options such as adjusting or replacing are covered separately in this module.

Items.Text: Accepting is the appropriate choice when the proposed structure aligns well with course requirements.
If significant changes are needed, learners should use the adjust or replace options rather than accepting prematurely.
Practicing the accept workflow builds confidence in recognizing a satisfactory AI-generated structure.

Topics.Title: Adjusting and Replacing the Module Breakdown
Topics.Summary: Focuses on how to modify individual modules or replace the entire AI-suggested structure with an alternative. Learners practice editing titles, reordering modules, and regenerating proposals.

Elements.Title: Editing Individual Module Titles
Elements.BodyText: After the AI proposes a module breakdown, learners can directly edit the title of any individual module to better reflect their course goals.
Elements.Notes: For example, an AI-suggested title like 'Introduction to Concepts' might be renamed to 'Core Principles Overview' to match the intended audience or tone.

Items.Text: Click on the module title field to activate inline editing and type the desired replacement name.
Edited titles are saved immediately as the module's display name; the underlying folder name stays stable so existing file paths keep working.
Custom titles help ensure the breakdown aligns with the specific learning objectives of the course.

Elements.Title: Reordering Modules in the Breakdown
Elements.BodyText: The sequence of modules in the AI-generated structure can be rearranged to create a more logical instructional flow.
Elements.Notes: Dragging Module 3 before Module 2, for instance, may better scaffold learner knowledge if prerequisite concepts appear earlier.

Items.Text: Use drag-and-drop or up/down controls to move a module to a new position in the list.
Reordering updates each module's stored order value; folder names are unchanged.
Reviewing the flow after reordering helps confirm that dependencies between modules are preserved.

Elements.Title: Modifying Individual Module Descriptions or Scope
Elements.BodyText: Beyond renaming, learners can adjust the scope or description of a single module without altering the rest of the breakdown.
Elements.Notes: This is useful when one AI-proposed module is too broad or too narrow compared to the others in the set.

Items.Text: Select the module to expand its detail panel, then edit the description or adjust the listed subtopics.
Narrowing or broadening a single module's scope keeps the overall structure intact while improving that section.
Changes to individual modules do not trigger a full regeneration of the entire breakdown.

Elements.Title: Replacing the Entire AI-Suggested Structure
Elements.BodyText: If the AI-proposed module breakdown does not meet course requirements, learners can discard it entirely and request a new proposal.
Elements.Notes: Replacing the full structure is appropriate when the source material was interpreted too narrowly, too broadly, or in the wrong domain focus.

Items.Text: Use the 'Regenerate' or 'Replace Breakdown' option to prompt PreseMaker to produce a completely new module structure.
Any manual edits made to the previous breakdown will be lost, so learners should save or note desired elements first.
Multiple regeneration attempts can be made until a satisfactory starting structure is produced.

Elements.Title: Regenerating a Proposal with Revised Inputs
Elements.BodyText: Learners can guide the regeneration by revising the module description or the source materials before requesting a new breakdown.
Elements.Notes: For example, adding more detail to your description or providing a clearer source steers the AI toward a more targeted structure.

Items.Text: Revise your description or source materials before triggering regeneration.
Adjusted parameters are passed back to the AI along with the original source material to refine the output.
Comparing the new proposal against the previous one helps learners identify which structure better serves their course design.

Elements.Title: Confirming and Locking the Final Breakdown
Elements.BodyText: Once the module structure has been adjusted or replaced to satisfaction, learners confirm the breakdown to lock it in as the basis for further course development.
Elements.Notes: Locking the breakdown creates the corresponding folder hierarchy on disk, making each module a distinct folder ready to receive content.

Items.Text: Review all module titles and their order one final time before confirming.
Confirming the breakdown commits the structure to the course's on-disk folder system.
After locking, individual modules can still be edited, but wholesale replacement requires starting the breakdown process again.

Topics.Title: Course and Module Storage as Folders on Disk
Topics.Summary: Explains how PreseMaker organizes courses and modules as a folder hierarchy on the local file system. Learners understand the relationship between the on-screen structure and the underlying file storage.

Elements.Title: Courses as Top-Level Folders
Elements.BodyText: In PreseMaker, each course you create is stored as a dedicated top-level folder on your local file system.
Elements.Notes: This means you can locate, back up, or move an entire course simply by working with its root folder in your operating system's file explorer.

Items.Text: The course folder is created automatically when you start a new course in PreseMaker.
The folder name typically corresponds to the course title you assign within the application.
All assets, settings, and content related to that course reside inside this single top-level folder.

Elements.Title: Modules as Subfolders Within the Course Folder
Elements.BodyText: Each module within a course is represented as a subfolder nested inside the parent course folder.
Elements.Notes: For example, a course folder named Intro_to_Safety contains one subfolder per module, each named after that module.

Items.Text: A module's folder is created when the module is created; renaming a module changes its display name, while the underlying folder name stays stable so existing file paths keep working.
Module order is tracked in the module's metadata, not in the folder name; each module folder is named after the module.
Removing a module takes it out of the course.

Elements.Title: Relationship Between On-Screen Structure and File Hierarchy
Elements.BodyText: The visual course and module tree displayed in PreseMaker directly mirrors the folder hierarchy stored on the local file system.
Elements.Notes: This one-to-one correspondence makes it straightforward to understand where content lives without needing to use PreseMaker itself to browse it.

Items.Text: Adding or removing a module changes the folders on disk; reordering and renaming update the module's metadata (order and display name) rather than folder names.
Conversely, manually altering folders outside PreseMaker without using the application may cause the on-screen structure to become out of sync.
Understanding this relationship helps learners troubleshoot missing content or unexpected structural issues.

Elements.Title: Contents Stored Inside a Module Subfolder
Elements.BodyText: Each module subfolder contains all the files needed to define and deliver that specific module's content.
Elements.Notes: This self-contained approach means a single module subfolder can be inspected, archived, or transferred independently of the rest of the course.

Items.Text: Source material files, generated topic content, and module configuration data are all stored within the module's subfolder.
Media assets such as images or documents referenced by a module are typically stored in dedicated asset directories within the same subfolder.
PreseMaker reads these files each time the module is opened, ensuring the interface reflects the current state of the folder contents.

Elements.Title: Practical Benefits of the Folder-Based Storage Model
Elements.BodyText: Organizing courses and modules as folders on disk provides learners and authors with transparent, portable, and easily manageable content storage.
Elements.Notes: Authors familiar with file system navigation will find it easy to integrate PreseMaker projects into existing version control or backup workflows.

Items.Text: Courses can be shared with collaborators by simply copying or compressing the top-level course folder.
Standard file system tools — such as search, version control systems, or backup utilities — work naturally with the folder hierarchy.
The flat, human-readable folder structure reduces dependency on proprietary databases and makes content recovery straightforward.
